name: Epics, Songs and Silver Screens: India's Storytellers
description: From the Ramayana and the Mahabharata to Bollywood and the films of Satyajit Ray: how India has told its stories in verse, stone, song and film.

checkpoints.name: The great epics
checkpoints.note: The Ramayana and the Mahabharata, both composed over centuries, carry tales of exile, war and duty that are still told across India and much of Asia. The Bhagavad Gita, a dialogue set inside the Mahabharata, becomes one of the best-known texts of Hindu thought.

checkpoints.name: Courts and monuments
checkpoints.note: Kalidasa's play Abhijnanashakuntalam, from around the fifth century, is among the best-loved dramas in Sanskrit. The Mughal emperor Shah Jahan has the Taj Mahal built from 1632, largely finished by about 1653, while in Amritsar the Golden Temple becomes the holiest shrine of the Sikhs.

checkpoints.name: Press and poetry
checkpoints.note: Printing presses and newspapers spread new writing across India. Rabindranath Tagore, born in 1861, writes poems, songs and plays in Bengali, and in 1913 becomes the first person outside Europe to win the Nobel Prize in Literature.

checkpoints.name: Talkies and new waves
checkpoints.note: The first Hindi talking film arrives in 1931, and Bollywood grows up in the studios of Bombay. Satyajit Ray's Pather Panchali (1955) wins praise abroad, Mother India (1957) is a huge hit, and the singer Lata Mangeshkar and the sitar player Ravi Shankar become known around the world.

checkpoints.name: Blockbusters and television
checkpoints.note: Sholay (1975) becomes one of the best-loved adventure films in India and makes a star of Amitabh Bachchan. The television serial Ramayan (1987) draws enormous audiences, Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge (1995), with Shah Rukh Khan, plays for years in a Mumbai cinema, and Lagaan (2001) is nominated for an Academy Award.
